ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Fannie Lou Hamer

code.originalText: Six-week review: blood pressure, kidney function and potassium after the new medicines, lipids, retinal photographs, and benefits

text.paragraph: Six-week review: blood pressure, kidney function and potassium after the new medicines, lipids, retinal photographs, and benefits. [S]

Mrs. Hamer returns six weeks after starting amlodipine-benazepril and dapagliflozin. Her home readings have come down to an average of 138/86. She has had no dizziness, cough, ankle swelling or genital itching. The potassium and creatinine check planned one to two weeks after the new medicines did not happen: the neighbor who was to drive her could not, the health center's van did not run to her road that week, and she did not want to ask again. SNAP has been approved; the energy assistance is pending. She went to the first diabetes class. She agreed today to blood tests and to retinal photographs once the camera was explained, and asked to see the pictures. [S]

Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). Improving, not yet at goal; the medicines have had six weeks. [S]

Community health worker to collect home readings by phone in four weeks; increase the dose if the average stays above 130/80.

Chronic kidney disease G2 A2 (N18.2). Potassium 4.7 mmol/L and creatinine 1.04 mg/dL (eGFR 66, a fall of under 10% from 73): the expected small change after starting benazepril and dapagliflozin, not harm. [S]
Continue both medicines.
Future checks on her clinic days, with rides arranged in advance, or a home blood draw.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 80 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40 mg, from 146; goal below 70. ALT 26 U/L. She did not want another pill now. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg; revisit a higher dose or ezetimibe at the yearly panel, her choice.
